correctness.rationale: For the unweighted full isotropic cone, the characters indexed by B are a basis (a nonzero F_q-linear bivector functional is surjective, even for a nonprime field). Each nonzero wedge has exactly q(q²−1) ordered presentations of determinant one. Independently, for each u!=0 sum the character over v in u^(perp_Omega): it totals q^(n−1) precisely when B(u,.) is proportional to Omega(u,.), and otherwise zero. Subtract the q multiples of u for every u!=0. The nonzero proportional vectors are a disjoint union of the nonzero radicals of B+tOmega. This gives lambda_B=[q^(n−2)(sum_t q^(2s_t)−q(q+1))+1]/(q²−1), as in the original proof. Alternating rank is even also in characteristic two, hence the formula is q^(n−2)(J−1)−delta with integer J>=0. Since 0<2delta<q^(n−2), only J=1 attains the smallest permitted magnitude, and J=1 is exactly one corank-two pencil member with all others invertible. An m-by-m nilpotent single Jordan block N yields an alternating off-diagonal pencil with blocks N^T+tI and −(N+tI); its lone singular member has corank two, in every characteristic. The positive row sum (q^n−1)delta is attained at B=0 and is a norm upper bound by the triangle inequality. Unitary Fourier diagonalization gives positive least singular value and condition number q^n−1. A fresh direct proportional-vector tally through all 4095 nonzero vectors for the Jordan witness at (q,n)=(4,6) found 15 proportional vectors, giving −17 against row sum 69615 by the per-vector count; this is finite corroboration in a nonprime field within scope.
residual_risks: Not a complete spectral multiplicity computation, nor a result for weighted or incomplete cones. Dimension-four tests in the frozen evidence are outside the theorem scope.

evidence: In ambient dimension n, equation (2) gives (q+1)eta=q^(n−3)N_1+(q^n−1)(q^(n−3)−1)/(q−1)^2. By Lemma 3.1 and rank parity, N_1=sum_t (q^(2s_t)−1)/(q−1)=(q+1)J. Substitution into q eta−L gives exactly q^(n−2)(J−1)−delta. Thus the evaluation, congruence, and conditional equality if J=1 need no new theorem from the older count.

The inspected minimum-distance witness has two singular pencil members and realizes maximum eta, not J=1. The frozen nilpotent construction realizes J=1 for every q,n in scope, not just a candidate spacing bound or a computed case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier formula yields a lower bound and necessary-and-sufficient profile for attaining that bound, but gives no witness or realized least singular value without solving the additional pencil feasibility problem. No inspected theorem or exact table was found to give that uniform attainment. The distinction is between allowed and realized distance from zero; the supported originality is the realized sharp boundary, not rederivation of the transform.

evidence: The matching Resultary 6d2a9c8e9364 is the target itself. Resultary 91dfe0fce2d0 concerns the ordinary Plücker cone; its proof gives the exact normalized character sum for any alternating frequency of specified rank. Orthogonality filters the fixed Omega=0 slice by averaging at B+tOmega, so it covers the sliced multiplier as an immediate corollary.

In Cardinali–Giuzzi arXiv:1503.05456, a projective support line contributes q−1 if B vanishes and −1 otherwise. Thus lambda=(q−1)L−q wt = q eta−L, where L is the number of isotropic projective lines and eta the number also isotropic for B. Nearest-zero magnitude corresponds to weight nearest (q−1)L/q, not minimum positive weight.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The character sum and projective weight are interchangeable descriptions, so a relevant exact weight or attainment theorem would count as coverage even if it did not mention inverses. The ordinary-cone identity and slice reduction already cover the underlying evaluation, not the realized nearest-zero level.

originality.rationale: Credit is limited to the sharp all-field nearest-zero endpoint, including its attainment and least-stable frequency characterization (and their conditioning interpretation), as distinguished in the frozen prior-work section. The per-frequency sliced multiplier itself is already implicit in two inspected sources; neither the isotropic point count, the arithmetic step, nor the row sum carries separate originality credit. The actual older theorems give a different extremum or do not give realizability at the nearest-to-zero level.
residual_risks: The multiplier is demonstrably already implicit in prior work; this pass does not credit it as new. Earlier pencil classifications or as-yet uninspected code weights may also imply attainment. No available statement in the compared literature was found to do so; the unavailable original rank-scheme text was not treated as negative evidence.

value.rationale: Once the entire nonzero isotropic Plücker cone is used, the natural question for inversion is how close its additive Fourier multipliers come to zero, not how large the projective section can be. Sharp all-field attainment quantifies stability on counting l² exactly, including characteristic two, and identifies the pencil profile of the least stable components. This adds an extremal fact not supplied by the exact but profile-conditional count or by code minimum distance; the standard counting argument alone is not the value claim.
residual_risks: No value claim about all spectral multiplicities, arbitrary apertures, weighted kernels, or improved inversion algorithms.
